newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says won't bow to Arab pressure.
newsitem.headline: Israel says won't bow to Arab pressure.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Sunday in response to Arab League condemnation of Israeli settlement policies that Arabs could not dictate Israeli policy through pressure.
"It is unacceptable that every time a problem arises in the peace process there is an attempt to exert pressure on Israel and to dictate its steps," Levy told Israel's Channel One television.
"With pressure it is impossible to defeat us...dialogue is the important thing because we all want peace," he added.
In Cairo, the Arab League on Sunday condemned Israel's expansion of settlements in the occupied West Bank and warned the Jewish state such practices could torpedo Middle East peace.

"Israel is endangering the peace process with settlements, which are considered against international law and are totally rejected by Arab countries and the world community," Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid told a news conference.
As the Arab League met, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed that the Jordan Valley area of the West Bank would be part of Israel forever.

Netanyahu has angered Arabs by his rejection of trading Arab lands occupied in the 1967 Middle East war and also by lifting a freeze on settlement building imposed by the dovish government he ousted in May.
More than 130,000 Jews live amid nearly two million Palestinians in settlements among the self-rule areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
The PLO set up autonomous enclaves in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under an interim deal with Israel signed in 1993.
Settlements were to be discussed at final status talks under an interim peace deal signed by Israel's previous government and the PLO in September 1993. The talks have yet to start under Netanyahu.
